analysis: The PR only modifies docs/architecture/inference.md. The patch adds a paragraph after the chat-template render check section (head lines 1118-1128) and a failure-mode table row (head line 1517). No executable code, keys, wire protocol or cache storage change in this diff. The documented behavior is that a restricted-effort template (Flash-Next, Qwen3.8-27B) accepts only low/medium/xhigh. Other active efforts return a typed HTTP 400 client_error before Jinja rendering, and media preparation rethrows typed request errors instead of wrapping them as retryable 503s. This is described as a provider-side input validation improvement, so it reduces the chance that consumer-controlled input is misclassified as a provider fault (500) and could taint routing health or reputation. The documentation does not weaken any threat-model assumption in TB-002, TB-007 or T-041. The error is content-free and typed, with no prompt data in the diagnostic. The sanitizedInferenceFailure and 400 mapping in ProviderLoop+ErrorMapping were not supplied. I could not verify that the code behind Qwen4SupportPolicy.validateReasoningContext matches the described behavior. That implementation is outside this docs-only diff. Remaining integration question: whether the actual code change that accompanies the docs preserves the error-sanitization contract and avoids echoing request content in the 400 message. Nothing in the supplied evidence shows a security regression. The coverage limit is that I only saw the docs, not the implementation.
